5 Things Every Lowcountry Homeowner Should Do Before Summer Ends

Summer in the Lowcountry can be tough on your landscape. Between intense heat, humidity, heavy rain, storms, and long growing seasons, your lawn, trees, and landscape beds can take a beating.

As summer winds down and fall approaches, now is the perfect time to give your property some attention. A little preventative maintenance can help your landscape recover from summer stress and prepare for the months ahead.

Here are 5 things every Lowcountry homeowner should do before summer ends.

1. Give Your Lawn Some Attention

Your lawn works hard during the hot South Carolina summer. Heat, foot traffic, weeds, insects, disease, and inconsistent watering can all leave grass looking thin, brown, or stressed.

Before summer ends, take a close look at your lawn for:

  • Bare or thinning areas
  • Weeds
  • Brown or discolored patches
  • Signs of insects or lawn disease
  • Compacted soil
  • Areas that aren’t receiving enough water

Proper mowing and irrigation are especially important during this transition period. Avoid cutting your grass too short, and make sure your irrigation system is providing adequate coverage without overwatering.

If your lawn has struggled throughout the summer, early fall can also be a good time to evaluate whether sod replacement or other lawn improvements are needed.

2. Check Your Irrigation System

Your irrigation system has likely been working overtime all summer.

Before you move into fall, take a few minutes to inspect your system, or have a professional irrigation company inspect it.

Look for:

  • Broken or clogged sprinkler heads
  • Leaking pipes or valves
  • Sprinklers watering sidewalks or driveways
  • Dry spots in the lawn
  • Areas receiving too much water
  • Incorrect controller settings

Even one malfunctioning sprinkler head can leave part of your landscape stressed while wasting water somewhere else.

A properly functioning irrigation system helps protect your investment in grass, plants, trees, and landscape beds while keeping your property looking its best.

3. Inspect Your Trees

Summer storms and strong winds can leave trees with damaged or weakened branches that aren’t always obvious from the ground.

Before fall arrives, inspect your trees for:

  • Dead branches
  • Cracked or hanging limbs
  • Broken branches
  • Leaning trees
  • Branches growing toward your home
  • Limbs hanging over driveways or outdoor living areas
  • Signs of disease or decay

Large trees near homes, vehicles, pools, fences, and power lines deserve particular attention.

Professional tree trimming and tree inspections can help identify potential hazards before they become expensive problems.

And if summer storms have damaged your trees, don’t wait until the next storm to address them.

4. Refresh Your Mulch

Summer heat and heavy rainfall can cause mulch to break down, wash away, or become uneven.

Refreshing your mulch before fall is an easy way to give your landscape an instant improvement while providing important benefits for your plants.

Mulch can help:

  • Retain soil moisture
  • Regulate soil temperature
  • Reduce weed growth
  • Protect plant roots
  • Improve the appearance of landscape beds

A fresh layer of quality mulch can make tired landscape beds look clean and finished while helping your plants transition into the next season.

Just remember that more mulch isn’t always better. Mulch should be applied properly around plants and trees rather than piled against trunks.

5. Clean Up Your Landscape

Finally, give your property a thorough end-of-summer cleanup.

Remove dead plants, fallen branches, excessive leaves, weeds, and other debris from your landscape beds and lawn.

This is also a great time to:

  • Prune overgrown shrubs
  • Remove dead annuals
  • Clean up planting beds
  • Trim back plants that have become overgrown
  • Clear debris from drainage areas
  • Remove storm-damaged branches
  • Touch up areas that have become neglected during the summer

A clean landscape not only looks better, it makes it easier to identify problems before they become bigger issues.

Don’t Forget Your Outdoor Living Spaces

Before temperatures begin to cool, take a look at the areas where your family spends time outdoors.

Inspect your paver patios, walkways, outdoor kitchens, fire pits, landscape lighting, and other hardscape features. Cleaning and addressing small problems now can help keep your outdoor spaces ready for fall entertaining.

Fall is one of the best times of year to enjoy the outdoors in the Lowcountry, so make sure your backyard is ready.

Get Your Lowcountry Landscape Ready for Fall

The transition from summer to fall is the perfect opportunity to evaluate your property and take care of small issues before they become bigger, and more expensive problems.

From lawn maintenance and irrigation service to tree trimming, mulch installation, landscape cleanup, and complete landscape improvements, preventative care can make a major difference in the health and appearance of your property.
